# GoodMem Java SDK Reference

Generated from the published `ai.pairsys:goodmem-java` 0.1.7 sources jar (Maven Central) —
every signature, parameter description, and return type below is parsed from
`goodmem-java-0.1.7-sources.jar`. OpenAI-style surface: every operation is
`client.<namespace>.<method>(...)` on a `Goodmem` (sync) or `AsyncGoodmem`
(async) instance.

## Dependency

Requires JDK 21+. Brings in OkHttp 4.12.0 and Jackson 2.18.2
(databind, jdk8, jsr310) transitively.

```xml
<!-- pom.xml -->
<dependency>
    <groupId>ai.pairsys</groupId>
    <artifactId>goodmem-java</artifactId>
    <version>0.1.7</version>
</dependency>
```

```kotlin
// build.gradle.kts
dependencies {
    implementation("ai.pairsys:goodmem-java:0.1.7")
}
```

## Client construction and auth

Read credentials from environment variables — never hardcode keys:

- `GOODMEM_BASE_URL` — server URL, e.g. `http://localhost:8080`
- `GOODMEM_API_KEY` — API key starting with `gm_`, sent as the `x-api-key` header

```java
import ai.pairsys.goodmem.client.Goodmem;

try (Goodmem client = Goodmem.builder()
        .baseUrl(System.getenv("GOODMEM_BASE_URL"))
        .apiKey(System.getenv("GOODMEM_API_KEY"))
        .timeout(java.time.Duration.ofSeconds(60))   // optional; default 30s
        .build()) {
    // use client
}
```

Builder contract (`Goodmem.builder()` / `AsyncGoodmem.builder()` — identical):

| Method | Notes |
|---|---|
| `baseUrl(String)` | Required. Null/empty URL throws `IllegalArgumentException` at `build()`. |
| `apiKey(String)` | Optional only for the bootstrap endpoints `system.info()` / `system.init()`; every other call returns 401 -> `AuthenticationException` without it. |
| `timeout(Duration)` | Connect/read/write timeout for the SDK-built OkHttp client (default 30s). Increase for RAG retrieval with LLM generation. Incompatible with `httpClient(...)` — combining them throws at `build()`. |
| `httpClient(OkHttpClient)` | BYO mode: pass a pre-configured `OkHttpClient` (interceptors, proxy, custom TLS). You own its lifecycle; configure timeouts on your own client. |

`Goodmem` implements `AutoCloseable` — prefer try-with-resources. The
SDK-built client disables redirect following (a redirect would carry
`x-api-key` across hosts); BYO clients control their own redirect policy.

Namespaces on the client (public final fields): `admin`, `apikeys`, `embedders`, `llms`, `memories`, `ocr`, `ping`, `rerankers`, `spaces`, `system`, `users`.

## SDK conventions

**Models are Java records** with Jackson annotations; camelCase wire names;
null fields are omitted from payloads. Every request/options record exposes a
nested builder (`XxxRequest.builder()....build()`); `Map<String,String>`
fields named `labels` also get a singular `label(key, value)` append setter.

**Typed IDs.** Resource ids are typed handles — `ApiKeyId`, `ChunkId`, `DeletedById`, `EmbedderId`, `LlmId`, `MemoryId`, `PolicyId`, `RerankerId`, `ResultSetId`, `SpaceId`, `TargetId`, `UserId`, `WorkerId` — each a record
wrapping the id string: `SpaceId.from(String)`, `SpaceId.from(UUID)`,
`.asUuid()`, and `toString()` returns the bare id. **Every method that takes
a resource id accepts `String`, `java.util.UUID`, or the typed handle; those
promotion overloads exist for every documented method below and are not
listed individually.**

**oneOf models** enforce "exactly one variant set" in their constructors and
expose static factories per variant (e.g. `ChunkingConfiguration.recursive(...)`,
`RetrievedItem.memory(...)` / `RetrievedItem.chunk(...)`); violating the
contract throws `IllegalArgumentException`.

**Typed options and raw escape hatches.** List/get methods take a typed
options record (or no argument for no filters); each also has a `listRaw` /
`getRaw` sibling accepting a raw `Map<String, Object>` for wire keys the
typed options don't yet expose.

**Media types.** `ai.pairsys.goodmem.client.MediaTypes` holds common
`contentType` constants: `TEXT_PLAIN`, `TEXT_MARKDOWN`, `TEXT_HTML`, `TEXT_CSV`, `APPLICATION_JSON`, `APPLICATION_PDF`, `APPLICATION_OCTET_STREAM`, `APPLICATION_XML`, `APPLICATION_NDJSON`, `IMAGE_PNG`, `IMAGE_JPEG`, `IMAGE_WEBP`, `IMAGE_TIFF`, `AUDIO_MPEG`, `AUDIO_WAV`, `VIDEO_MP4`.

## Streaming and pagination

- `memories.retrieve(...)` returns a `RetrieveMemoryStream` — an
  `Iterable<RetrieveMemoryEvent>` that is also `AutoCloseable` (NDJSON over
  `POST /v1/memories:retrieve`). Always consume in try-with-resources; the
  iterator can be drained only once. `ping.stream(...)` returns a `PingStream`
  of `PingEvent` with the same contract.
- Paginating list endpoints (`spaces.list`, `memories.list`, `memories.pages`,
  `admin.retrieveMemoryLogPoliciesList`) return a lazy
  `ai.pairsys.goodmem.client.Page<T>`: `items()` (current page only),
  `hasMore()` / `nextToken()`, `next()` (throws `NoSuchElementException` when
  exhausted), `iterator()` (lazy cross-page iteration over everything, usable
  once), and `iterator(long maxItems)`. Embedders/LLMs/rerankers/API keys
  return plain `List`s.

```java
// Idiomatic: for-each transparently walks every page
for (Memory m : client.memories.list(spaceId)) {
    System.out.println(m.memoryId() + " " + m.processingStatus());
}
```

## Async client

`AsyncGoodmem` mirrors `Goodmem` exactly (same builder, namespaces, close
semantics); every method returns `CompletableFuture<T>`. Paginating list
endpoints return `CompletableFuture<AsyncPage<T>>` — `AsyncPage` exposes
`items()`, `hasMore()`, `nextToken()` synchronously and `next()` as
`CompletableFuture<AsyncPage<T>>` (not `Iterable`; chain with `thenCompose`).
`memories.retrieve` returns `CompletableFuture<RetrieveMemoryStream>`; the
future completes when stream headers arrive. Async errors complete the future
exceptionally with the same typed exceptions, wrapped in
`CompletionException` — unwrap with `ex.getCause()`.

```java
import ai.pairsys.goodmem.client.AsyncGoodmem;

try (AsyncGoodmem client = AsyncGoodmem.builder()
        .baseUrl(System.getenv("GOODMEM_BASE_URL"))
        .apiKey(System.getenv("GOODMEM_API_KEY"))
        .build()) {

    client.memories.retrieve(RetrieveMemoryRequest.builder()
            .message("deployment checklist")
            .spaceId(spaceId)
            .build())
        .thenAccept(events -> {
            try (events) {
                for (RetrieveMemoryEvent e : events) {
                    if (e.abstractReply() != null) {
                        System.out.println(e.abstractReply().text());
                    }
                }
            }
        })
        .join();
}
```

## Errors

All SDK exceptions are unchecked and live in `ai.pairsys.goodmem.client.errors`. `ApiException` exposes `getStatusCode()` and `getBody()`; `RateLimitException` adds `getRetryAfterSeconds()` (nullable `Long`). `IllegalArgumentException` signals client-side misuse (null required arguments, invalid oneOf combinations, out-of-range values) and is thrown before any request is sent.

- `GoodmemException` (extends RuntimeException) — Root of the GoodMem SDK exception hierarchy. Catch this to handle any SDK-raised failure — HTTP errors (`ApiException` and its typed subclasses), transport-level failures (`NetworkException`), or SDK-internal validation that the client refuses to send to the server.
- `ApiException` (extends GoodmemException) — Base class for any HTTP 4xx / 5xx returned by the GoodMem server. Concrete subclasses cover the common statuses (`BadRequestException` 400, `AuthenticationException` 401, `PermissionDeniedException` 403, `NotFoundException` 404, `ConflictException` 409, `UnprocessableEntityException` 422, `RateLimitException` 429, `InternalServerException` 5xx); a status that doesn't match a typed subclass is raised as a plain `ApiException`.
- `NetworkException` (extends GoodmemException) — Wraps a transport-level failure (DNS, connect, read/write, timeout, mid-stream drop). Mirrors Python's `NetworkError`: callers can catch transport failures specifically without losing the `GoodmemException` parent type, so existing `catch (GoodmemException)` branches still work.
- `AuthenticationException` (extends ApiException) — HTTP 401 Unauthorized — the API key is missing, malformed, or has been revoked. Construct a fresh `Goodmem` client with a valid key and retry.
- `BadRequestException` (extends ApiException) — HTTP 400 Bad Request — the server rejected the request shape (a required field was omitted, a value violated a server-side range check, mutually exclusive fields were both set, etc.). The exception message embeds the server's diagnostic text; `getBody` has the full payload.
- `ConflictException` (extends ApiException) — HTTP 409 Conflict — the request collides with existing server state. Most often raised on idempotent `create` retries: when a caller supplies a stable `memoryId` / `spaceId` / `apiKeyId` that already exists, the first request creates the resource and subsequent retries surface as 409 ALREADY_EXISTS rather than producing duplicates. Treat as a successful idempotent retry.
- `NotFoundException` (extends ApiException) — HTTP 404 Not Found — the resource referenced by the request id doesn't exist (or was deleted). Idempotent `delete` retries may legitimately encounter this; call sites that treat delete as fire-and-forget should swallow it.
- `PermissionDeniedException` (extends ApiException) — HTTP 403 Forbidden — the API key authenticates but lacks the permission required for this operation (e.g. attempting `CREATE_MEMORY_ANY` without admin scope, or accessing a private space owned by another user without `READ_MEMORY_ANY`). Distinct from `AuthenticationException`, which means the credential itself is invalid.
- `RateLimitException` (extends ApiException) — HTTP 429 Too Many Requests — the caller (or the upstream provider the server is proxying to, e.g. an LLM/embedder) exceeded its rate limit. Back off and retry.
- `UnprocessableEntityException` (extends ApiException) — HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity — the request was syntactically well-formed but failed semantic validation (e.g. a temperature outside the LLM's accepted range, an embedder model identifier the provider doesn't recognize). Distinct from `BadRequestException` (HTTP 400), which signals shape errors the SDK should ideally have caught client-side.
- `InternalServerException` (extends ApiException) — HTTP 5xx — the server failed to handle a well-formed request (database error, embedder timeout, retrieval pipeline failure, etc.). Treat as a transient failure: retrying with backoff is appropriate for idempotent operations. The message and `getBody` carry the server's diagnostic so logs can surface a meaningful cause.

```java
import ai.pairsys.goodmem.client.errors.*;

try {
    Memory m = client.memories.get(memoryId);
} catch (NotFoundException e) {
    // handle missing memory
} catch (RateLimitException e) {
    Long retryAfter = e.getRetryAfterSeconds();  // may be null
} catch (ApiException e) {
    System.err.println("HTTP " + e.getStatusCode() + ": " + e.getBody());
}
```

## End-to-end example

```java
import ai.pairsys.goodmem.client.ChatPostProcessorConfig;
import ai.pairsys.goodmem.client.Goodmem;
import ai.pairsys.goodmem.client.RetrieveMemoryStream;
import ai.pairsys.goodmem.client.models.*;

try (Goodmem client = Goodmem.builder()
        .baseUrl(System.getenv("GOODMEM_BASE_URL"))
        .apiKey(System.getenv("GOODMEM_API_KEY"))
        .build()) {

    // Embedder: provider API key from the environment; the bundled model
    // registry fills provider type, endpoint, and dimensionality.
    EmbedderResponse embedder = client.embedders.create(
        EmbedderCreationRequest.builder()
            .displayName("default-embedder")
            .modelIdentifier("text-embedding-3-small")
            .build(),
        System.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY"));

    Space space = client.spaces.create(
        SpaceCreationRequest.builder()
            .name("project-notes")
            .label("env", "prod")
            .spaceEmbedders(java.util.List.of(
                new SpaceEmbedderConfig(embedder.embedderId(), null)))
            .build());

    // Text memory (contentType auto-fills to "text/plain")
    client.memories.create(JsonMemoryCreationRequest.builder()
        .spaceId(space.spaceId())
        .originalContent("The staging cluster runs Kubernetes 1.29.")
        .metadata(java.util.Map.of("source", "runbook"))
        .build());

    // Upload a PDF from disk (base64-encodes, infers content type)
    client.memories.create(space.spaceId(), java.nio.file.Path.of("report.pdf"));

    // Plain semantic retrieval (streaming)
    try (RetrieveMemoryStream events =
            client.memories.retrieve("which Kubernetes version?", space.spaceId())) {
        for (RetrieveMemoryEvent evt : events) {
            if (evt.retrievedItem() != null && evt.retrievedItem().chunk() != null) {
                System.out.println(evt.retrievedItem().chunk().chunk().chunkText());
            }
        }
    }

    // RAG: retrieve -> rerank -> generate via the built-in chat post-processor
    RetrieveMemoryRequest req = RetrieveMemoryRequest.builder()
        .message("Summarize what we know about the staging cluster")
        .spaceId(space.spaceId())
        .requestedSize(10)
        .postProcessor(ChatPostProcessorConfig.builder()
            .llmId(System.getenv("GOODMEM_LLM_ID"))
            .llmTemp(0.2)
            .genTokenBudget(2048L)
            .build())
        .build();
    try (RetrieveMemoryStream events = client.memories.retrieve(req)) {
        for (RetrieveMemoryEvent evt : events) {
            if (evt.abstractReply() != null) {
                System.out.println(evt.abstractReply().text());   // generated answer
            }
        }
    }
}
```

### client.admin

#### `admin.backgroundJobsPurge(AdminPurgeJobsRequest request) -> AdminPurgeJobsResponse`

Purge completed background jobs

Deletes terminal background jobs older than a retention cutoff.

Parameters:
- `request` (`AdminPurgeJobsRequest`): request payload — see `AdminPurgeJobsRequest` for the field-level contract.

Returns: the `AdminPurgeJobsResponse` response.

#### `admin.drain(AdminDrainRequest request) -> AdminDrainResponse`

Request the server to enter drain mode

Initiates drain mode and optionally waits for the server to quiesce.

**Convenience override:** validates the body-budget against the client's read timeout before issuing the request, failing fast with an actionable message when they don't compose. Connection-level timeouts live on the client — widen via `Goodmem.builder().timeout(...)` for long-running ops. See `inv-budget-exceeds-client-timeout-fails-fast`.

Parameters:
- `request` (`AdminDrainRequest`): request payload — see `AdminDrainRequest` for the field-level contract.

Returns: the `AdminDrainResponse` response.

#### `admin.licenseReload() -> AdminReloadLicenseResponse`

Reload the active license from disk

Triggers the server to reload its license file from the configured directory and returns metadata about the currently active license.

Returns: the `AdminReloadLicenseResponse` response.

#### `admin.retrieveMemoryLogPoliciesCreate(CreateRetrieveMemoryLogPolicyRequest request) -> RetrieveMemoryLogPolicy`

Create a RetrieveMemory log policy

Creates an immutable administrative policy that can automatically enable durable RetrieveMemory request logging.

Parameters:
- `request` (`CreateRetrieveMemoryLogPolicyRequest`): request payload — see `CreateRetrieveMemoryLogPolicyRequest` for the field-level contract.

Returns: the `RetrieveMemoryLogPolicy` response.

- `request` (`DeleteRetrieveMemoryLogPolicyRequest`): request payload — see `DeleteRetrieveMemoryLogPolicyRequest` for the field-level contract.

#### `admin.retrieveMemoryLogPoliciesGet(String id, Map<String, Object> query) -> RetrieveMemoryLogPolicy`

Get a RetrieveMemory log policy

Retrieves a live RetrieveMemory log policy by UUID, or a tombstoned policy when includeDeleted is true.

Parameters:
- `id` (`String`): path segment for `id`; must be a non-empty `String` (empty values are rejected before the request is sent).
- `query` (`Map<String, Object>`): raw query parameters as a `Map<String, Object>`; `null` or empty sends no filters. Prefer the typed `XxxOptions` sibling for compile-time safety; `Raw` suffix marks this as the escape hatch.

Returns: the `RetrieveMemoryLogPolicy` response.

#### `admin.retrieveMemoryLogPoliciesList(Map<String, Object> query) -> Page<RetrieveMemoryLogPolicy>`

List RetrieveMemory log policies

Lists RetrieveMemory log policies with optional tombstone, active-time, name, label, sort, and pagination filters. LABEL FILTERS: Label filters accept either label.<key>=<value> or label[key]=value (for example, label.environment=production or label[environment]=production).

Parameters:
- `query` (`Map<String, Object>`): raw query parameters as a `Map<String, Object>`; `null` or empty sends no filters. Prefer the typed `XxxOptions` sibling for compile-time safety; `Raw` suffix marks this as the escape hatch.

Returns: a paginated lazy `Page` of `RetrieveMemoryLogPolicy` that iterates across all pages on demand. Calling `items()` returns only the current page.

Request and option types used by `client.admin`:

**`AdminDrainRequest`** Build with `AdminDrainRequest.builder()`.

- `timeoutSec` (`Integer`): Maximum seconds to wait for the server to quiesce before returning.
- `reason` (`String`): Human-readable reason for initiating drain mode.
- `waitForQuiesce` (`Boolean`): If true, wait for in-flight requests to complete and the server to reach QUIESCED before responding.

**`AdminPurgeJobsRequest`** Build with `AdminPurgeJobsRequest.builder()`.

- `olderThan` (`String`): ISO-8601 timestamp cutoff; only terminal jobs older than this instant are eligible.
- `statuses` (`List<PurgeableBackgroundJobStatus>`): Optional terminal background job statuses to target for purging. If omitted, all terminal statuses are eligible. Canonical values are BACKGROUND_JOB_SUCCEEDED, BACKGROUND_JOB_FAILED, and BACKGROUND_JOB_CANCELED. Short aliases SUCCEEDED, FAILED, and CANCELED are also accepted for compatibility.
- `dryRun` (`Boolean`): If true, report purge counts without deleting any rows.
- `limit` (`Integer`): Maximum number of jobs to purge in this request. Must be >= 0; 0 means no limit.

**`CreateRetrieveMemoryLogPolicyRequest`** — REST request for creating an immutable RetrieveMemory log policy. Build with `CreateRetrieveMemoryLogPolicyRequest.builder()`. Extra builder setters: `label(...)`.

- `policyId` (`PolicyId`): Optional client-provided policy UUID. Typed wrapper `PolicyId`; build from a raw string with `PolicyId.from`.
- `displayName` (`String`): Human-readable policy name.
- `description` (`String`): Optional operator description.
- `condition` (`RetrieveMemoryLogPolicyCondition`): Policy match condition.
- `activeFrom` (`Long`): Inclusive activation time in milliseconds since epoch.
- `activeUntil` (`Long`): Exclusive deactivation time in milliseconds since epoch.
- `labels` (`Map<String, String>`): Operator labels for listing and administration.

**`DeleteRetrieveMemoryLogPolicyRequest`** — Optional REST body for tombstoning a RetrieveMemory log policy. Build with `DeleteRetrieveMemoryLogPolicyRequest.builder()`.

- `reason` (`String`): Optional tombstone reason.

### client.apikeys

#### `apikeys.create(CreateApiKeyRequest request) -> CreateApiKeyResponse`

Create a new API key

Creates a new API key for authenticating with the API. New keys start in ACTIVE status and can be used immediately for authentication. The response includes the one-time raw API key value which will not be retrievable later - clients must save this value as it cannot be recovered. Requires CREATE_APIKEY_OWN permission (or CREATE_APIKEY_ANY for admin users). Side effects include generating cryptographically secure key material, recording creation timestamp, and tracking creator ID. Returns INVALID_ARGUMENT if expires_at is set to a time in the past.

Parameters:
- `request` (`CreateApiKeyRequest`): request payload — see `CreateApiKeyRequest` for the field-level contract.

Returns: the `CreateApiKeyResponse` response.

#### `apikeys.delete(String id)`

Delete an API key

Permanently deletes an API key. This operation cannot be undone and immediately invalidates the key for all future authentication attempts. TIP: For reversible deactivation, use PUT /v1/apikeys/{id} with status=INACTIVE instead. Requires DELETE_APIKEY_OWN permission for keys you own (or DELETE_APIKEY_ANY for admin users to delete any user's keys). Side effects include permanently removing the key record from the database and immediate authentication invalidation.

Parameters:
- `id` (`String`): path segment for `id`; must be a non-empty `String` (empty values are rejected before the request is sent).

#### `apikeys.list() -> List<ApiKeyResponse>`

List API keys

Retrieves a list of API keys belonging to the authenticated user. The list includes metadata about each key but not the actual key values or key hashes for security reasons. Requires LIST_APIKEY_OWN permission (or LIST_APIKEY_ANY for admin users to view keys from any user). This is a read-only operation with no side effects.

Returns: the unwrapped `List` of `ApiKeyResponse` items.

#### `apikeys.update(String id, UpdateApiKeyRequest request) -> ApiKeyResponse`

Update an API key

Updates an existing API key with new values for status or labels. IMPORTANT: Key ID, user ownership, key material, and audit fields cannot be modified - only status (ACTIVE/INACTIVE) and labels are mutable. Requires UPDATE_APIKEY_OWN permission for keys you own (or UPDATE_APIKEY_ANY for admin users to modify any user's keys). Side effects include updating the updated_at timestamp and recording the updater's user ID. This operation is idempotent - repeated identical requests have no additional effect.

Parameters:
- `id` (`String`): path segment for `id`; must be a non-empty `String` (empty values are rejected before the request is sent).
- `request` (`UpdateApiKeyRequest`): request payload — see `UpdateApiKeyRequest` for the field-level contract.

Returns: the `ApiKeyResponse` response.

Request and option types used by `client.apikeys`:

**`CreateApiKeyRequest`** — Request parameters for creating a new API key. Build with `CreateApiKeyRequest.builder()`. Extra builder setters: `label(...)`.

- `labels` (`Map<String, String>`): Key-value pairs of metadata associated with the API key. Used for organization and filtering.
- `expiresAt` (`Long`): Expiration timestamp in milliseconds since epoch. If not provided, the key does not expire.
- `apiKeyId` (`ApiKeyId`): Optional client-provided UUID for idempotent creation. If not provided, server generates a new UUID. Returns ALREADY_EXISTS if ID is already in use. Typed wrapper `ApiKeyId`; build from a raw string with `ApiKeyId.from`.

**`UpdateApiKeyRequest`** — Request parameters for updating an API key. Build with `UpdateApiKeyRequest.builder()`.

- `status` (`UpdateApiKeyRequestStatus`): New status for the API key. Allowed values: ACTIVE, INACTIVE. Typed enum `UpdateApiKeyRequestStatus`; unknown server values fail Jackson deserialization loudly. Values: `ACTIVE`, `INACTIVE`.
- `replaceLabels` (`Map<String, String>`): Replace all existing labels with this set. Mutually exclusive with mergeLabels.
- `mergeLabels` (`Map<String, String>`): Merge these labels with existing ones. Mutually exclusive with replaceLabels.

### client.embedders

#### `embedders.create(EmbedderCreationRequest request) -> EmbedderResponse`

Create a new embedder

Creates a new embedder configuration for vectorizing content. Embedders represent connections to different embedding API services (like OpenAI, vLLM, etc.) and include all the necessary configuration to use them with memory spaces. DUPLICATE DETECTION: Returns HTTP 409 Conflict (ALREADY_EXISTS) if another embedder exists with identical {ownerId, providerType, endpointUrl, apiPath, modelIdentifier, dimensionality, distributionType, credentialsFingerprint} after URL canonicalization. Uniqueness is enforced per-owner, allowing different users to have identical configurations. Credentials are hashed (SHA-256) for uniqueness while remaining encrypted. The apiPath field defaults to '/v2/embed' for Cohere, '/embed' for TEI, and '/embeddings' for other providers when omitted. Requires CREATE_EMBEDDER_OWN permission (or CREATE_EMBEDDER_ANY for admin users).

**Convenience override:** applies declarative transforms (registry lookup, endpoint inference, default injection, credential check as declared for this method in convenience.json) before forwarding to the raw Tier-2 request. Any field already set on `request` wins.

Parameters:
- `request` (`EmbedderCreationRequest`): request payload — see `EmbedderCreationRequest` for the field-level contract.

Returns: the `EmbedderResponse` response.

#### `embedders.create(EmbedderCreationRequest request, String apiKey) -> EmbedderResponse`

Convenience overload: auto-fills provider / endpoint / dimensionality from the bundled model registry keyed by `modelIdentifier`, and converts a bare `apiKey` string to the structured `EndpointAuthentication`. Pass `null` for `apiKey` to preserve `request.credentials()`. Any field already set on `request` wins over registry values.

Parameters:
- `request` (`EmbedderCreationRequest`): creation request; required fields filled from the registry when null.
- `apiKey` (`String`): raw provider API key wired into the request's `credentials` field; pass `null` to keep an already-set `request.credentials()`.

Returns: the created `EmbedderResponse`

#### `embedders.delete(String id)`

Delete an embedder

Permanently deletes an embedder configuration. This operation cannot be undone and removes the embedder record and securely deletes stored credentials. IMPORTANT: This does NOT invalidate or delete embeddings previously created with this embedder - existing embeddings remain accessible. CONFLICT: Returns HTTP 409 Conflict if the embedder is still referenced by a space. Requires DELETE_EMBEDDER_OWN permission for embedders you own (or DELETE_EMBEDDER_ANY for admin users).

Parameters:
- `id` (`String`): path segment for `id`; must be a non-empty `String` (empty values are rejected before the request is sent).

#### `embedders.get(String id) -> EmbedderResponse`

Get an embedder by ID

Retrieves the details of a specific embedder configuration by its unique identifier. Requires READ_EMBEDDER_OWN permission for embedders you own (or READ_EMBEDDER_ANY for admin users to view any user's embedders). This is a read-only operation with no side effects.

Parameters:
- `id` (`String`): path segment for `id`; must be a non-empty `String` (empty values are rejected before the request is sent).

Returns: the `EmbedderResponse` response.

#### `embedders.list(EmbedderListOptions options) -> List<EmbedderResponse>`

List embedders

Retrieves a list of embedder configurations accessible to the caller, with optional filtering. LABEL FILTERS: Label filters accept either label.<key>=<value> or label[key]=value (for example, label.environment=production or label[environment]=production). PERMISSION-BASED FILTERING: With LIST_EMBEDDER_OWN permission, you can only see your own embedders (ownerId filter is ignored if set to another user). With LIST_EMBEDDER_ANY permission, you can see all embedders or filter by any ownerId. This is a read-only operation with no side effects. **Typed-options overload.** See `EmbedderListOptions` for the available filter fields. Passing `null` is equivalent to an empty filter set.

Parameters:
- `options` (`EmbedderListOptions`): typed options — see `EmbedderListOptions` below; passing `null` sends no filters

Returns: the unwrapped `List` of `EmbedderResponse` items.

Other overloads:
- `embedders.listRaw(Map<String, Object> query) -> List<EmbedderResponse>` — raw query-map escape hatch — prefer the typed overload
- `embedders.list() -> List<EmbedderResponse>` — no filters

#### `embedders.update(String id, UpdateEmbedderRequest request) -> EmbedderResponse`

Update an embedder

Updates an existing embedder configuration including display information, endpoint configuration, model parameters, credentials, and labels. All fields are optional - only specified fields will be updated. IMPORTANT: providerType is IMMUTABLE after creation and cannot be changed. CRITICAL: Returns HTTP 412 Precondition Failed (FAILED_PRECONDITION) if attempting to update core fields (dimensionality, distributionType, modelIdentifier) while the embedder is actively referenced by spaces or ingestion jobs. #### `memories.create(JsonMemoryCreationRequest request) -> Memory`

Create a new memory

Creates a new memory in a specified space and starts asynchronous processing. The memory begins in PENDING status while a background job performs chunking and embedding generation. IDEMPOTENCY: If memoryId is omitted, the server generates a new UUID and retries are not idempotent. If the client supplies a stable memoryId, the operation behaves as create-if-absent: the first request creates the memory and subsequent retries return HTTP 409 Conflict (ALREADY_EXISTS) rather than creating duplicates. Returns INVALID_ARGUMENT if space_id, original_content, or content_type is missing or invalid. Returns NOT_FOUND if the specified space does not exist. Requires CREATE_MEMORY_OWN permission for spaces you own (or CREATE_MEMORY_ANY for admin users to create in any space). Side effects include creating the memory record and enqueuing a background processing job.

**Convenience override:** when `request.originalContent() != null` and `request.contentType() == null`, fills `contentType="text/plain"` before delegating to the Tier-2 base. Mirrors Python's auto-inference for the most common text-content case.

- `request` (`JsonMemoryCreationRequest`): request payload — see `JsonMemoryCreationRequest` for the field-level contract.

Returns: the `Memory` response.

### client.rerankers

#### `rerankers.create(RerankerCreationRequest request) -> RerankerResponse`

Create a new reranker

Creates a new reranker configuration for ranking search results. Rerankers represent connections to different reranking API services (like TEI, OpenAI, etc.) and include all the necessary configuration to use them for result ranking. DUPLICATE DETECTION: Returns HTTP 409 Conflict (ALREADY_EXISTS) if another reranker exists with identical {ownerId, providerType, endpointUrl, apiPath, modelIdentifier, credentialsFingerprint} after URL canonicalization. Uniqueness is enforced per-owner, allowing different users to have identical configurations. Credentials are hashed (SHA-256) for uniqueness while remaining encrypted. DEFAULTS: apiPath defaults to '/v2/rerank' for Cohere and '/rerank' for other providers if omitted; supportedModalities defaults to [TEXT] if omitted. Requires CREATE_RERANKER_OWN permission (or CREATE_RERANKER_ANY for admin users). This operation is NOT idempotent - each request creates a new reranker record.

**Convenience override:** applies declarative transforms (registry lookup, endpoint inference, default injection, credential check as declared for this method in convenience.json) before forwarding to the raw Tier-2 request. Any field already set on `request` wins.

Parameters:
- `request` (`RerankerCreationRequest`): request payload — see `RerankerCreationRequest` for the field-level contract.

Returns: the `RerankerResponse` response.

#### `rerankers.create(RerankerCreationRequest request, String apiKey) -> RerankerResponse`

Convenience overload: auto-fills provider / endpoint / dimensionality from the bundled model registry keyed by `modelIdentifier`, and converts a bare `apiKey` string to the structured `EndpointAuthentication`. Pass `null` for `apiKey` to preserve `request.credentials()`. Any field already set on `request` wins over registry values.

Parameters:
- `request` (`RerankerCreationRequest`): creation request; required fields filled from the registry when null.
- `apiKey` (`String`): raw provider API key wired into the request's `credentials` field; pass `null` to keep an already-set `request.credentials()`.

Returns: the created `RerankerResponse`

#### `rerankers.delete(String id)`

Delete a reranker

Permanently deletes a reranker configuration. This operation cannot be undone and immediately removes the reranker record from the database. SIDE EFFECTS: Invalidates any cached references to this reranker; does not affect historical usage data or audit logs. Requires DELETE_RERANKER_OWN permission for rerankers you own (or DELETE_RERANKER_ANY for admin users). This operation is safe to retry - may return NOT_FOUND if already deleted.

Parameters:
- `id` (`String`): path segment for `id`; must be a non-empty `String` (empty values are rejected before the request is sent).

#### `rerankers.get(String id) -> RerankerResponse`

Get a reranker by ID

Retrieves the details of a specific reranker configuration by its unique identifier. Response payloads include stored credentials, matching gRPC response semantics. Requires READ_RERANKER_OWN permission for rerankers you own (or READ_RERANKER_ANY for admin users). This is a read-only operation with no side effects and is safe to retry.

Parameters:
- `id` (`String`): path segment for `id`; must be a non-empty `String` (empty values are rejected before the request is sent).

Returns: the `RerankerResponse` response.

#### `rerankers.list(RerankerListOptions options) -> List<RerankerResponse>`

List rerankers

Retrieves a list of reranker configurations accessible to the caller, with optional filtering. IMPORTANT: Pagination is NOT supported - all matching results are returned. Results are ordered by created_at descending. Responses include stored credentials, matching gRPC response semantics. LABEL FILTERS: Label filters accept either label.<key>=<value> or label[key]=value (for example, label.environment=production or label[environment]=production). PERMISSION-BASED FILTERING: With LIST_RERANKER_OWN permission, only your own rerankers are shown. With LIST_RERANKER_ANY permission, you can see all rerankers or filter by any ownerId. Specifying ownerId without LIST_RERANKER_ANY permission returns PERMISSION_DENIED. **Typed-options overload.** See `RerankerListOptions` for the available filter fields. Passing `null` is equivalent to an empty filter set.

Returns: the unwrapped `List` of `RerankerResponse` items.

Update a reranker

Updates an existing reranker configuration including display information, endpoint configuration, model parameters, credentials, and labels. All fields are optional - only specified fields will be updated. IMMUTABLE FIELDS: providerType and ownerId cannot be changed after creation. SUPPORTED_MODALITIES UPDATE: If the array contains >=1 elements, it replaces the stored set; if empty or omitted, no change occurs and it does not count as an update by itself. Returns ALREADY_EXISTS if update would create duplicate with same {ownerId, providerType, endpointUrl, apiPath, modelIdentifier, credentialsFingerprint} after URL canonicalization (HTTP 409 Conflict / ALREADY_EXISTS). Requires UPDATE_RERANKER_OWN permission for rerankers you own (or UPDATE_RERANKER_ANY for admin users). This operation is idempotent.

- `ownerId` (`UserId`): Filter spaces by owner ID. With LIST_SPACE_ANY permission and ownerId omitted, returns all visible spaces. Otherwise returns caller-owned spaces only. Specifying ownerId without LIST_SPACE_ANY returns PERMISSION_DENIED.
- `nameFilter` (`String`): Filter spaces by name using glob pattern matching
- `maxResults` (`Integer`): Maximum number of results to return in a single page (defaults to 50, clamped to [1, 1000])
- `nextToken` (`String`): Pagination token for retrieving the next set of results
- `sortBy` (`SpacesListSortBy`): Field to sort by: 'created_time', 'updated_time', or 'name' (default: 'created_time'). Unsupported values return INVALID_ARGUMENT. Values: `CREATED_TIME`, `UPDATED_TIME`, `NAME`.
- `sortOrder` (`SortOrder`): Sort order (ASCENDING or DESCENDING, default: DESCENDING). Values: `ASCENDING`, `DESCENDING`, `SORT_ORDER_UNSPECIFIED`.
- `label` (`Map<String, String>`): Filter by label key-value pairs. Label filters accept either label.<key>=<value> or label[key]=value (for example, label.environment=production or label[environment]=production).

**`UpdateSpaceRequest`** — Request parameters for updating a space. Build with `UpdateSpaceRequest.builder()`.

- `name` (`String`): The new name for the space.
- `publicRead` (`Boolean`): Whether the space is publicly readable by all users.
- `replaceLabels` (`Map<String, String>`): Labels to replace all existing labels. Mutually exclusive with mergeLabels.
- `mergeLabels` (`Map<String, String>`): Labels to merge with existing labels. Mutually exclusive with replaceLabels.

### client.system

#### `system.info() -> SystemInfoResponse`

Retrieve server build metadata

Returns the server's advertised semantic version, git metadata, build timestamp, and optional capability flags. The endpoint is intentionally unauthenticated so bootstrap tooling can call it before API keys exist.

Returns: the `SystemInfoResponse` response.

#### `system.init() -> SystemInitResponse`

Initialize the system

Initializes the system by creating a root user and API key. This endpoint should only be called once during first-time setup. If the system is already initialized, the endpoint will return a success response without creating new credentials.

Returns: the `SystemInitResponse` response.

### client.users

#### `users.get(UsersGetOptions opts) -> UserResponse`

Unified entry-point — the SOLE public `get` on this client. Mirrors Python's `client.users.get(id=..., email=...)` kwargs form and the AWS / GCP / Azure / OpenAI options-bag norm. The mutex (exactly one of the option fields must be set) is enforced in `UsersGetOptions`'s compact constructor.

Parameters:
- `opts` (`UsersGetOptions`): options bag selecting exactly one of the supported lookup keys; see `UsersGetOptions`.

Returns: the matched `UserResponse`

#### `users.me() -> UserResponse`

Get current user profile

Retrieves the authenticated user's profile information including email, display name, and creation time. This endpoint does not require any parameters as it automatically returns the caller's information.

Returns: the `UserResponse` response.

Request and option types used by `client.users`:

**`UsersGetOptions`** — Unified options for `users.get` — pass exactly one of `id` or `email`. Mirrors Python's `client.users.get(id=..., email=...)` kwargs form so the surface is symmetric across SDKs. Per the options-bag convention used by AWS SDK v2, GCP, and the OpenAI Java SDK, this is the single entry-point — there are no separate `get(String)` / `getByEmail(String)` overloads. Build with `UsersGetOptions.builder()`.

- `id` (`String`): user UUID (mutually exclusive with `email`)
- `email` (`String`): user email (mutually exclusive with `id`)
